katas.title: Order download: throw the domain exception for a missing order, like CheckoutService does

edits.replace:
var order = await orders.GetByIdAsync(orderId, cancellationToken).ConfigureAwait(false)
                ?? throw new DomainException("Order was not found.");

defects.scenario: A buyer (or a bot) requests GET /api/orders/{random-guid}/download for an order id that does not exist.
defects.find: ?? throw new DomainException("Order was not found.");
defects.consequence: The global handler maps every DomainException to 400 "Business rule violation" (Program.cs:56), so the one endpoint that returned a correct 404 now answers 400; clients can no longer tell "no such order" from "you sent something invalid".
One exception type for both rule violations and missing entities is review finding A; the patch spreads it instead of introducing a typed not-found error.

defects.scenario: The precedent the patch copies is itself the reviewed defect.
defects.find: ?? throw new DomainException("Order was not found for payment intent.");
defects.consequence: "Consistent with CheckoutService" is consistency with a known 404-as-400 bug (CheckoutService.cs:98).
